machineProject.name: USB mouse reuse study
machineProject.purpose: Develop a useful single-action USB foot control from an ordinary discarded wired mouse, without buying a development board. Compare alternatives and persist concrete engineering work; no physical specimen or measurements exist.

actions.action: Obtain actual donor identity, external condition, button positions and available reclaimed base/hinge/return materials. Report actual dimensions and provenance; do not import B100 envelope as specimen dimensions.

On a later authorized bench, establish enumeration and actual input reports; identify exactly one chosen button down/up pair and confirm release behavior. Capture OS/application and supported bindings.
Size an adjustable mouse cradle and independent pedal load path; set compliant pusher and positive stop using actual button force/travel evidence. No build dimensions established here.
Only if remote option remains needed, obtain unpowered switch-node continuity/topology evidence and reclaimed switch/wire/enclosure inventory before drawing any pin-level schematic.

Proposed later acceptance: 100 deliberate press/release cycles yield exactly 100 target actions and no extra events; 10-second hold yields one action then releases cleanly; no pointer/wheel/other-button events, slipping, cable pull or switch bottoming. These are proposed trial criteria, not lifetime proof or completed tests.
Retain this bounded plan until arbitrary mouse-controller and mechanical-only specs are supported or a measured donor contract exists. Do not repair into an invented catalog board to pass HS.

host_behavior.mapping: Use native application mouse-button binding if available. A keyboard-only target requires device-specific host remapping, subject to later OS/application evidence.
host_behavior.single_action: One target application action on the chosen button down transition; suppress repeat while held; re-arm after release.
host_behavior.unwanted_inputs: Mount against translation; shield unused buttons and wheel; verify zero unwanted pointer/wheel/other button actions in target use.

mechanical_design.adjustment: Adjust mouse locating blocks, pusher position and stop only after actual envelope, button travel and allowable force are established. No dimensions are fabricated.
mechanical_design.load_path: Foot load goes through treadle, hinge and positive hard stop into a broad nonslip base; mouse shell/button is not the structural end stop.
mechanical_design.protection: Guard wheel and other buttons, retain cable strain relief, avoid pinch points; removal should restore ordinary mouse use.
mechanical_design.return: Independent treadle return bias must release the pusher; do not rely on the mouse switch to lift the pedal.

proposed_design.system_boundary: Reuse original mouse USB cable/controller/firmware; no purchased development board and no firmware modification.

electrical_design.connection_rule: No pad numbers, common-ground assumption, pullup voltage or pinout asserted. Before a schematic, establish switch terminal function and open/closed topology with unpowered traceable evidence.
electrical_design.contact_rule: Only if evidence confirms an isolated dry-contact equivalent, propose a passive normally-open contact across the verified original button closure nodes. Never inject external voltage or connect USB supply/data wires to the pedal.
electrical_design.routing: Keep USB cable and electronics unchanged; evaluate added wire length, strain relief, short protection and switch bounce after donor evidence.
